roadmap.scope: bug fix (nw-bugfix Phase 3) — root cause: comments::show_issue omits the CSRF double-submit issuance seam (cookie mint + hidden _csrf field) that every other write-form page uses, so both forms on the issue page fail csrf_middleware with 'CSRF token missing or mismatched'.

steps.name: Regression test + fix: the add-comment form carries a usable CSRF token
criteria: RED: rewire the add-comment CSRF acquisition so the token comes from the REAL issue page, not GET /sign-in. Today crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/us_10_comments.rs (around the sign-in CSRF fetch) hand-mints the token from /sign-in and injects it into the form, bypassing the bug. Change it (or add a distinct @csrf scenario in tests/features/us-10-comments.feature) to: GET /team/{team}/project/{project}/issues/{n}; capture foundry_csrf from that GET's Set-Cookie; scrape input[name=_csrf] from the add-comment form via the scraper crate; POST the comment using ONLY that cookie + scraped token. Must FAIL against current code (no Set-Cookie / no hidden field -> 403 or panic on the missing field). Capture the RED evidence.

GREEN: factor ensure_csrf_cookie + response_with_optional_cookie into crate::csrf as pub(crate) and repoint issues.rs to use them (remove issues.rs private copies); dedupe keyboard.rs's copy too if a trivial repoint, else leave and note it.
GREEN: add pub csrf: String to IssuePage in crates/foundry-app/src/views.rs.

GREEN: add a hidden <input type=hidden name=_csrf value={{ csrf }}> as the first child of the add-comment <form> in crates/foundry-app/templates/issue.html (view-model + template edits must land together; askama fails to compile {{ csrf }} without the field).

GREEN: add headers: HeaderMap to show_issue in crates/foundry-app/src/comments.rs; call ensure_csrf_cookie(&state, &headers); thread the token through render_issue_page into IssuePage.csrf; return via response_with_optional_cookie(StatusCode::OK, Html(...).into_response(), set_cookie).
The new/hardened comment scenario passes AND the existing us-10 comment scenarios stay green.
cargo fmt --all --check and cargo clippy --all-targets --release -D warnings are clean.
steps.scenario_name: The add-comment form carries a usable CSRF token

steps.name: Regression test + fix: CSRF-protect the attachment upload form
criteria: RED: add an acceptance scenario proving the server contract that makes the browser upload workable: GET the issue page -> it sets foundry_csrf -> a multipart upload POST carrying x-csrf-token = that cookie value succeeds. Against current code this fails because the issue-page GET sets no cookie to mirror (the reqwest harness sends the header directly; it is not a browser, so this pins the server side; the browser JS gesture is dogfooded, same split as board-dnd.js). Reuse the multipart upload helper idiom in feature_remaining_surfaces.rs / us_11_attachments.
GREEN: the cookie-mint from 01-01 already satisfies the server side; verify the scenario passes with that alone.

GREEN: add the browser JS hook so a real user's upload works: a small CSP-safe static script (new crates/foundry-app/static/js/csrf-upload.js, or extend board-dnd.js if cleaner) that on submit of the multipart upload form reads the foundry_csrf cookie and sends the multipart body via fetch with the x-csrf-token header (surface error on non-2xx), mirroring board-dnd.js's cookie->header idiom; wire it in templates/base.html (defer); serve it with the same revalidating cache header the other app-owned JS uses (commit e248506) so edits reach browsers.
GREEN: add a cheap acceptance assertion that the script is served (mirror card-ranking's 'the drag-and-drop script is served' scenario).
No regressions across the comment, attachment, and web scenarios; cargo fmt + release clippy clean; a full cargo xtask ci is run at the end by the orchestrator.
steps.scenario_name: The issue page CSRF-protects the attachment upload
